'''Mike McGuire''' (born July 21, 1979) is an American [[politician]] who has been a member of the [[California State Senate]] representing the [[California's 2nd State Senate district|2nd district]] since 2014. A [[California Democratic Party|Democrat]], he served as majority leader from 2022 to 2024 and [[president pro tempore of the California State Senate|senate president pro tempore]] from 2024 to 2025. His district encompasses the [[North Coast (California)|North Coast]] region, from [[Marin County, California|Marin County]] to [[Del Norte County, California|Del Norte County]].

McGuire served as assistant majority leader from 2018 until he succeeded [[Robert Hertzberg]] as majority leader in 2022.<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 19, 2022 |title=Our State Senate Representative, Mike McGuire, Just Got Named Majority Leader |url=https://lostcoastoutpost.com/2022/jan/19/our-state-senate-rep-mike-mcguire-just-got-named-m/ |work=Lost Coast Outpost}}</ref> Prior to being elected to the state senate in 2014, he was a member of the [[Sonoma County Board of Supervisors]] and served as mayor of [[Healdsburg, California|Healdsburg]].<ref>{{cite news|work=The Press Democrat |date=May 16, 2014 |url=http://www.pressdemocrat.com/news/1863054-181/pd-editorial-mike-mcguire-is |title= PD Editorial: Mike McGuire is best choice in Senate election |first=Beth |last=Schlanker }}</ref> By August 2023, he began fundraising to run for [[California Insurance Commissioner|State Insurance Commissioner]] in 2026.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Graham |first=Andrew |date=August 8, 2023 |title=As term limits push McGuire from state Senate, is a run for insurance chief next? |url=https://www.pressdemocrat.com/article/news/mike-mcguire-reports-fundraising-for-statewide-office-of-insurance-commissi/ |access-date=April 11, 2024 |location=Santa Rosa |work=The Press Democrat |language=en-US}}</ref> By November 2025, McGuire changed course and announced that he would instead run for Congress in the newly redrawn [[California's 1st congressional district|1st district]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.pressdemocrat.com/2025/11/13/i-want-to-earn-every-vote-mike-mcguire-announces-run-for-congress-in-redrawn-north-coast-district/|title=‘I want to earn every vote’: Mike McGuire announces run for Congress in redrawn North Coast district|date=November 13, 2025}}</ref> He had also run in the [[2026 California's 1st congressional district special election|special election]] for the same district in 2026 with the existing boundaries but had lost to [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[James Gallagher (California politician)|James Gallagher]] by a wide margin.<ref>{{cite news |title=Republican James Gallagher wins special election for vacant red House district in California |first=Ben |last=Kamisar |website=NBC News |date=June 2, 2026 |access-date=June 2, 2026 |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/republican-james-gallagher-wins-special-election-vacant-red-house-dist-rcna348179}}</ref>

==Early life, education, and career==

Mike McGuire comes from a family of farmers, specializing in grape and prune farming for over 50 years. In 1998, he became the youngest person ever elected to the [[Healdsburg, California|Healdsburg]] [[School Board]] at age 19.<ref>{{cite news |work=The Point Reyes Light |date=March 20, 2014 |url=http://www.ptreyeslight.com/article/mike-mcguire-his-election-assured-remains-little-known-marin |title=Mike McGuire, his election assured, remains little known in Marin |first=Herb |last=Kutchins}}</ref> He attended [[Sonoma State University]] in [[Rohnert Park, California]], receiving a Bachelor of Arts in [[political science]] in 2002.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://news.sonoma.edu/article/mcguire-distinguished-alum|title=McGuire Distinguished Alum|date=December 21, 2016|work=SSU News|access-date=November 23, 2017|language=en}}</ref>

McGuire first held elected office at 19 in 1998 when he was elected to the Healdsburg School Board.{{citation needed|date=November 2023}} In 2004, he was elected to the [[Healdsburg, California|Healdsburg]] [[City Council]], where he spent six years, including time as the city's youngest mayor.<ref name=":0">California State Senate Majority Caucus [http://sd02.senate.ca.gov/biography California Senator Mike McGuire ''Senate District 2'' Biography]</ref> In 2010, he became a member of the [[Sonoma County, California|Sonoma County]] [[Board of Supervisors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sonomacounty.ca.gov/Board-of-Supervisors/Press-Releases/2013/Supervisor-Mike-McGuire-Hosts-Annual-Windsor-Town-Hall-Meeting-on-August-19th/|title=Supervisor Mike McGuire Hosts Annual Windsor Town Hall Meeting on August 19th|website=sonomacounty.ca.gov|language=en|access-date=November 23, 2017}}</ref>

==California State Senate==

In 2014, McGuire ran for the California State Senate to succeed Democratic senator [[Noreen Evans]], who decided not to seek reelection. McGuire easily defeated [[California Republican Party|Republican]] candidate Lawrence Weisner for the District 2 State Senate seat that year, winning 70% of the vote.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://ballotpedia.org/California_State_Senate_elections,_2014|title=California State Senate elections, 2014 - Ballotpedia|access-date=November 23, 2017|language=en-US}}</ref>

In April 2015, he introduced bill SB 643, with the purpose of legalizing and regulating the [[Medical cannabis|medical marijuana]] industry.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billStatusClient.xhtml?bill_id=201520160SB643|title=Bill Status|website=leginfo.legislature.ca.gov|access-date=November 23, 2017}}</ref> The regulation would cover cultivation to consumption.<ref>{{cite news|work=Ukiah Daily Journal |date=April 30, 2015 |url=http://www.ukiahdailyjournal.com/general-news/20150430/california-sen-mike-mcguire-proposes-regulating-medical-marijuana-industry |title=California Sen. Mike McGuire proposes regulating medical marijuana industry}}</ref> McGuire criticized the state's lack of rules and regulations for medical marijuana,<ref>{{cite news|work=The Guardian |date=May 3, 2015 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2015/may/03/california-law-and-order-medical-marijuana-market |title=California looks to bring law and order to decades-old medical marijuana market |first=Anita |last=Chabria }}</ref> and was opposed to the [[Adult Use of Marijuana Act]] (Proposition 64).<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.sonomanews.com/news/6250108-181/citing-marijuana-mess-sen-mike|title=Citing marijuana 'mess,' Sen. Mike McGuire opposes California's faulty Proposition 64|website=Sonoma News |date=October 31, 2016|author=Guy Kovner|access-date=February 2, 2019}}</ref> In September 2017, he was part of the state's legislative session that urged Congress to [[censure]] the president [[Donald Trump]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.politico.com/story/2017/09/17/california-tears-into-trump-242801|title=California tears into Trump|website=Politico |date=September 17, 2017|author=David Siders|access-date=February 2, 2019}}</ref>

In September 2018, the bill he introduced to establish a statewide protocol for emergency alerts for all 58 California counties was signed into a law.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.pressdemocrat.com/news/8764585-181/gov-brown-signs-into-law|title=Gov. Brown signs into law California emergency alerts and wildfire liability bills|website=The Press Democrat |location=Santa Rosa |date=September 21, 2018|author=Guy Kovner|access-date=February 2, 2019}}</ref> In December 2018, he was selected to serve as assistant majority leader of the California Senate.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.pressdemocrat.com/news/9098396-181/healdsburg-democrat-mike-mcguire-appointed?sba=AAS|title=Healdsburg Democrat Mike McGuire appointed to a top California Senate leadership post |website=The Press Democrat |location=Santa Rosa |date=December 22, 2018|author=Julie Johnson|access-date=February 2, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://krcrtv.com/north-coast-news/eureka-local-news/sen-mike-mcguire-named-assistant-majority-leader-of-ca-state-senate|title=Sen. Mike McGuire named assistant majority leader of CA State Senate|publisher=KRCR-TV |location=Redding |date=December 24, 2018|author=Marissa Papanek|access-date=February 2, 2019}}</ref> In early January 2019, McGuire "applauded" Governor [[Gavin Newsom]]'s 2019 budget plan for California.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.northcoastjournal.com/NewsBlog/archives/2019/01/10/wood-mcguire-applaud-govs-budget-plan|title=Wood, McGuire Applaud Gov.'s Budget Plan|website=North Coast Journal |date=January 10, 2019|author=Thadeus Greenson|access-date=February 2, 2019}}</ref> That same month, when President Donald Trump threatened to withhold government emergency fundings for the wildfires because of poor forest management by the state of California, McGuire replied in a tweet that most California forests affected are managed by the federal government and not the state.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.times-standard.com/2019/01/09/trump-blames-california-wildfires-on-forest-mismanagement/|title=Trump, California lawmakers spar over wildfire funding|newspaper=Times-Standard|date=January 9, 2019|access-date=February 2, 2019}}</ref>

In 2019, he co-authored [[California Senate Bill 27]] (SB27) officially named ''Tax Transparency Bill'' which was signed into law by Newsom on July 30, 2019.<ref>{{cite press release |url= https://www.gov.ca.gov/2019/07/30/governor-gavin-newsom-signs-sb-27-tax-transparency-bill/ |title=Governor Gavin Newsom Signs SB 27: Tax Transparency Bill|date=July 30, 2019 |publisher=Office of the Governor of California}}</ref> He authored a bill that established the [[Great Redwood Trail]] as a proposed rail-to-trail project in Northern California.<ref>{{cite news |last=Wear |first=Kimberly |date=February 3, 2022 |title=Moving Up |url=https://www.northcoastjournal.com/humboldt/moving-up/Content?oid=22682866 |access-date=June 20, 2022 |website=North Coast Journal |language=en-us}}</ref>

McGuire was announced as the incoming State Senate President Pro-Tempore on August 28, 2023.<ref>{{cite news |last=Luna |first=Taryn |date=August 29, 2023 |title=California Senate taps new leader |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2023-08-28/california-senate-taps-new-leader-toni-atkins-mike-mcguire |access-date=August 30, 2023 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> He assumed the position on February 5, 2024.

As President pro tempore of the California State Senate, McGuire selected Sen. María Elena Durazo to lead the Senate Local Government Committee and Aisha Wahab to lead the Senate Housing Committee. Both Durazo and Wahab used their chairmanship to seek to block the passage of California state legislation to allow apartment buildings near major transportation hubs in California, amid a major housing shortage.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 1, 2025 |title=California Democrats Split on Bills to Promote Housing |url=https://www.governing.com/urban/california-democrats-split-on-bills-to-promote-housing |website=Governing |language=en}}</ref>

== Candidacy for U.S. House ==
{{main|2026 California's 1st congressional district special election|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in California (districts 1–26)#District 1}}
In 2026, McGuire ran for the open seat for [[California's 1st congressional district]] in the United States House of Representatives made vacant after the death of [[Doug LaMalfa]].<ref name="Gallagher">{{Cite web |last=Mejia|first=Alejandro Mejia|date=2026-01-14|title=Assemblyman James Gallagher announces bid for District 1 seat|url=https://www.actionnewsnow.com/news/assemblyman-james-gallagher-announces-bid-for-district-1-seat/article_9a506ebb-d52b-4971-98ba-99eabdbf090d.html|access-date=2026-01-14|website=Action News Now|language=en}}</ref> He was defeated by Republican State Assemblyman [[James Gallagher (California politician)|James Gallagher]] in the [[2026 California's 1st congressional district special election|special election]] for the LaMalfa's remaining term.<ref>{{cite news |title=Republican James Gallagher wins special election for vacant red House district in California|first=Ben|last=Kamisar|website=NBC News|date=June 2, 2026|access-date=June 2, 2026|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/republican-james-gallagher-wins-special-election-vacant-red-house-dist-rcna348179}}</ref> The special election also coincided with the primary election under the new district boundaries following the passage of [[2025 California Proposition 50|Proposition 50]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shannon|first=Madeline|date=2026-10-12|title=Gallagher, McGuire seek Northern California seat in Congress|url=https://www.insidenova.com/news/gallagher-mcguire-seek-northern-california-seat-in-congress-943b0a025bc0|access-date=2026-10-25|website=InsideNoVa|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kallepalli|first=Nevin|date=2026-06-22|title=With James Gallagher as LaMalfa’s replacement, an ardent conservative will continue to represent California’s District 1 — for now|url=https://shastascout.org/with-james-gallagher-as-lamalfas-replacement-an-ardent-conservative-will-continue-to-represent-californias-district-1-for-now/|access-date=2026-10-25|website=Shasta Scout|language=en-US}}</ref> In this election, both Gallagher and McGuire advanced, setting up a rematch in the November general election in which McGuire is favored as the Democratic nominee.<ref>{{cite news |title=Gallagher leads in two 1st District races for Congress, with McGuire staking claim to runoff|first=Austin|last=Murphy|work=The Press Democrat|date=June 2, 2026|access-date=June 2, 2026|url=https://www.pressdemocrat.com/2026/06/02/gallagher-leads-in-two-1st-district-races-for-congress-with-mcguire-staking-claim-to-runoff/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-10-23|title=James Gallagher faces tough reelection fight in California’s 1st District|url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/james-gallagher-faces-tough-reelection-140000193.html|access-date=2026-10-25|website=Yahoo News|language=en-US}}</ref>

In the 2026 November general election, McGuire defeated incumbent James Gallagher following redistricting.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-11-03 |title=Mike McGuire wins California Congressional District 1 race, CBS News projects - CBS Sacramento |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/california-congressional-district-1-james-gallagher-mike-mcguire/ |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=www.cbsnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref>
